title: Long-term effects of therapeutic hypothermia following neonatal asphyxia – Analysis of contributing factors
summary:
Standardized management of infants during therapeutic hypothermia has a decisive impact on outcomes. We were able to demonstrate that treatment regimens vary considerably across different hospitals in Germany, despite the rarity of the condition. Therefore, in 2023 we established the German Hypothermia Registry. The initial aim of the registry was to assess the current status of cooled asphyxiated newborns in Germany and to establish a standardized treatment protocol. This protocol was developed in accordance with international standard treatment guidelines and has been rapidly adopted. Currently, more than 60 hospitals participate in the registry, and 200 cooled newborns have been registered to date. So far, it has been shown that treatment according to the proposed standardized protocol is feasible.

At present, only anonymized retrospective data are collected in the registry. Consequently, it has not been possible to assess long-term patient outcomes or to evaluate the benefits of standardized treatment. This is now intended to change, enabling the collection and analysis of long-term outcome data.

The data will be obtained from patients’ medical records. Study participants will be examined at standardized time points in the neonatal follow-up clinic up to 24 months of age. Assessments at 4 and 6/7 years of age will be conducted at the Social Pediatric Center as part of routine pediatric follow-up care. As this is a data analysis, no risks, disadvantages, or harm are to be expected.

The expected/planned sample size (total and locally to be included persons, maximum N = 100) is based on the following statistical considerations: The incidence of perinatal asphyxia is 1–3 per 1,000 live births. Data will be collected prospectively over a period of 10 years. With an annual birth rate of 2,500–3,000 deliveries at UKB, we expect a maximum of 100 patients over 10 years.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Participants will be newborns with a gestational age of ≥36 weeks who, from April 1, 2025 onward, fulfilled the postnatal criteria for perinatal asphyxia and were treated with therapeutic hypothermia. The criteria for perinatal asphyxia are:
i) postnatal pH ≤7.0 and/or base deficit ≥15 mmol/L measured in umbilical arterial blood or in a blood sample obtained within the first hour of life,
ii) Apgar score <5 at 10 minutes,
iii) cardiopulmonary resuscitation within the first 10 minutes of life.
In addition, signs of encephalopathy must be present (Sarnat score >1 or pathological amplitude-integrated EEG).
Exclusion criteria:
Preterm infants <30 weeks of gestation, as well as newborns ≥36 weeks of gestation who did not fulfill the postnatal asphyxia criteria or who had a congenital malformation or intracerebral hemorrhage, will be excluded.
